DZ.hint: Green and white halves split vertically, with a red crescent and star straddling the middle.
DZ.funFact: Algeria is the largest country in Africa by area.

AO.hint: Red over black, with a yellow half cog-wheel and machete crossed under a star.
AO.funFact: Portuguese is the official language, and Angola is one of Africa's biggest oil producers.

BJ.hint: Green vertical stripe on the left, yellow over red on the right, and no emblem at all.
BJ.funFact: Benin is the birthplace of the Vodun (voodoo) religion, celebrated with a national holiday every 10 January.

BW.hint: Light sky-blue with a black stripe edged in white across the middle, like a zebra crossing the sky.
BW.funFact: Botswana has the world's largest population of African elephants.

BF.hint: Red over green with a single yellow star in the centre.
BF.funFact: Its name means 'land of upright (honest) people', mixing words from two local languages.

BI.hint: A white X splits red and green triangles, with a white circle holding three red stars.
BI.funFact: The three stars stand for the national motto: Unity, Work, Progress.

CV.hint: Blue with a thin white-red-white stripe low down and a ring of ten yellow stars, one for each main island.
CV.funFact: The islands were uninhabited until Portuguese explorers arrived in the 1400s.

CM.hint: Green, red, yellow vertical stripes with a gold star on the red middle. Senegal's star is green.
CM.funFact: Cameroon is called 'Africa in miniature' because it has almost every African landscape and climate.

CF.hint: Four horizontal stripes (blue, white, green, yellow) crossed by one red vertical stripe, plus a yellow star in the corner.
CF.funFact: Its flag mixes French tricolour colours with pan-African colours to symbolise unity.

TD.hint: Blue, yellow, red vertical, almost identical to Romania! Chad's blue is a slightly darker indigo.
TD.funFact: Lake Chad has shrunk by around 90% since the 1960s.

KM.hint: Four stripes plus a green triangle holding a white crescent and four stars, one per island.
KM.funFact: Comoros is one of the world's top producers of ylang-ylang, a flower oil used in perfume.

CD.hint: Sky blue with a red diagonal stripe edged in yellow and a yellow star in the top-left.
CD.funFact: DR Congo is the most populous French-speaking country in the world.

CG.hint: A yellow diagonal band separates green (top-left) from red (bottom-right). No stars or emblems.
CG.funFact: Its capital Brazzaville faces DR Congo's capital Kinshasa across the Congo River, the closest pair of capitals after Rome and Vatican City.

CI.hint: Orange, white, green vertical: Ireland in reverse! Ivory Coast has orange at the flagpole.
CI.funFact: Ivory Coast is the world's largest producer of cocoa beans.

DJ.hint: Light blue over green with a white triangle holding a red star.
DJ.funFact: Lake Assal in Djibouti is the lowest point in Africa, about 155 m below sea level.

EG.hint: Red, white, black stripes with a golden eagle in the middle. Yemen has no emblem; Iraq has green writing.
EG.funFact: About 95% of Egyptians live close to the Nile River.

GQ.hint: Green, white, red stripes, a blue triangle, and a coat of arms with a tree and six stars.
GQ.funFact: It's the only country in Africa where Spanish is an official language.

ER.hint: A huge red triangle stretching across the whole flag between green and blue, with a golden olive wreath.
ER.funFact: Its capital Asmara is a UNESCO World Heritage Site for its Italian modernist buildings.

SZ.hint: A black-and-white Nguni shield and spears lying sideways across a wide crimson stripe.
SZ.funFact: Eswatini was called Swaziland until 2018 and is one of the world's last absolute monarchies.

ET.hint: Green, yellow, red stripes with a blue circle holding a yellow star. Green is on top.
ET.funFact: Ethiopia's green, yellow and red inspired the 'pan-African' colours used by many African nations.

GA.hint: Plain green, yellow, blue horizontal stripes.
GA.funFact: Almost 90% of Gabon is covered in rainforest.

GM.hint: Red and green stripes with a blue band edged in white through the middle: the Gambia River.
GM.funFact: The Gambia is the smallest country on mainland Africa and is almost completely surrounded by Senegal.

GH.hint: Red, yellow, green with a black star in the centre. The black star is the giveaway.
GH.funFact: Ghana was the first sub-Saharan African colony to win independence, in 1957.

GN.hint: Red, yellow, green vertical: Mali flipped! Guinea starts with red at the flagpole.
GN.funFact: Guinea has around a quarter of the world's known bauxite, the ore used to make aluminium.

GW.hint: Red vertical band with a black star, then yellow over green.
GW.funFact: Its Bijagós Archipelago of 88 islands is a UNESCO biosphere reserve.

KE.hint: Black, red, green stripes edged in white, with a red Maasai shield and two crossed spears.
KE.funFact: Kenya is named after Mount Kenya, Africa's second-highest mountain.

LS.hint: Blue, white, green stripes with a black Basotho straw hat in the middle.
LS.funFact: Lesotho is entirely surrounded by South Africa, and even its lowest point is about 1,400 m above sea level.

LR.hint: Looks like the USA flag but with only 11 stripes and one big white star.
LR.funFact: Founded by freed American slaves, Liberia became Africa's first republic in 1847.

LY.hint: Red, black, green stripes with a white crescent and star on the wide black middle.
LY.funFact: From 1977 to 2011 Libya's flag was plain green, the only single-colour national flag.

MG.hint: White vertical stripe on the left, red over green on the right.
MG.funFact: Around 90% of Madagascar's wildlife, including every lemur, lives nowhere else on Earth.

MW.hint: Black, red, green stripes with a red rising sun on the black top stripe.
MW.funFact: Lake Malawi has more species of fish than any other lake on Earth.

ML.hint: Green, yellow, red vertical: Guinea reversed! Mali has green at the flagpole.
ML.funFact: Timbuktu in Mali was a great centre of learning, and its ancient manuscripts are still preserved.

MR.hint: Green with a gold crescent and star, plus thin red bands at the top and bottom (added in 2017).
MR.funFact: The 'Eye of the Sahara', a 40 km wide rock formation visible from space, is in Mauritania.

MU.hint: Four equal horizontal stripes: red, blue, yellow, green.
MU.funFact: Mauritius was the only home of the dodo, which went extinct in the late 1600s.

MA.hint: Red with a green five-pointed star drawn as an outline. Vietnam's star is solid yellow.
MA.funFact: Morocco's University of al-Qarawiyyin, founded in 859, is considered the oldest existing university.

MZ.hint: The only national flag with a rifle: an AK-47 crossed with a hoe on a book, inside a red triangle.
MZ.funFact: Mozambique's Indian Ocean coastline stretches about 2,500 km.

NA.hint: A red diagonal band edged in white, a blue top corner with a golden 12-ray sun, and green at the bottom.
NA.funFact: The Namib Desert is thought to be the oldest desert in the world, at least 55 million years old.

NE.hint: Orange, white, green horizontal with an orange circle in the middle. India has a blue wheel instead.
NE.funFact: Niger is named after the Niger River, and about 80% of it lies in the Sahara Desert.

NG.hint: Simple green-white-green vertical stripes with nothing on them.
NG.funFact: Nigeria is Africa's most populous country, and its 'Nollywood' film industry is one of the biggest in the world.

RW.hint: A wide light-blue top with a golden sun in the top-right corner, above yellow and green stripes.
RW.funFact: Rwanda banned plastic bags in 2008 and is known as one of Africa's cleanest countries.

ST.hint: Green-yellow-green stripes with a red triangle and two black stars on the yellow.
ST.funFact: It's Africa's second-smallest country: two volcanic islands sitting almost on the equator.

SN.hint: Green, yellow, red vertical with a green star on the yellow middle. It's Mali with a star.
SN.funFact: Dakar, Senegal's capital, is the westernmost city on mainland Africa.

SC.hint: Five coloured rays fanning out from the bottom-left corner: blue, yellow, red, white, green.
SC.funFact: The Seychelles' coco de mer palm produces the heaviest seed of any plant, up to 25 kg.

SL.hint: Green, white, blue horizontal stripes. Gabon has yellow in the middle instead of white.
SL.funFact: Its capital Freetown was founded in 1792 as a home for freed slaves.

SO.hint: Light blue with one big white star in the middle.
SO.funFact: Somalia has the longest coastline of mainland Africa, about 3,000 km.

ZA.hint: A green sideways 'Y' shape with six colours: red top, blue bottom and a black triangle.
ZA.funFact: South Africa has three capitals: Pretoria (government), Cape Town (parliament) and Bloemfontein (courts).

SS.hint: Black, red, green stripes edged in white, with a blue triangle and a gold star.
SS.funFact: South Sudan is the world's youngest country, independent since 2011.

SD.hint: Red, white, black stripes with a green triangle on the flagpole side.
SD.funFact: Sudan has more ancient pyramids than Egypt: over 200, at sites like Meroë.

TZ.hint: A black diagonal stripe edged in yellow, with green top-left and blue bottom-right.
TZ.funFact: Tanzania is home to Mount Kilimanjaro, Africa's highest mountain.

TG.hint: Five green and yellow stripes with a red square and white star in the corner.
TG.funFact: The five stripes stand for the five regions of Togo.

TN.hint: Red with a white circle holding a red crescent and star. Türkiye's crescent sits loose on the red.
TN.funFact: The desert planet Tatooine in Star Wars was filmed in Tunisia.

UG.hint: Black, yellow, red stripes repeated twice, with a grey crowned crane in a white circle.
UG.funFact: Uganda is home to about half of the world's remaining mountain gorillas.

ZM.hint: Green with an orange eagle flying over three small vertical stripes (red, black, orange) in the bottom-right.
ZM.funFact: Victoria Falls, on the Zambia–Zimbabwe border, is one of the largest waterfalls on Earth.

ZW.hint: Seven stripes (green, yellow, red, black) with a white triangle holding the golden Zimbabwe Bird on a red star.
ZW.funFact: Zimbabwe is named after Great Zimbabwe, a medieval stone city whose bird carving is on the flag.
